newsitem.title: UK: Fund managers see mild UK impact from tobacco sale.
newsitem.headline: Fund managers see mild UK impact from tobacco sale.

text.p: Fund managers said on Wednesday they expect limited damage to British tobacco shares in the wake of a decision by Florida Pension fund trustees to order its portfolio managers to sell about $825 million of tobacco stocks.

"I think that the risk is less for the British tobacco companies because the litigation environment here is less extreme. The perceived market risk must be lower," said Ian Carstairs, head of UK equities at Invesco Asset Management.
Of major British tobacco companies, Imperial Tobacco and soon-to-be-floated Gallaher have no U.S. exposure, while B.A.T. Industries is owner of US firm Brown & Williamson.
"Litigation was bad news 12 or 18 months ago, but I think it is largely factored into the prices now," said Mike Bishop, head of UK Equities at Gartmore Investment Management.
But Carstairs said that the Florida decision might have an effect if tobacco shares are hit in New York. "I think to a large extent the UK on tobacco stocks takes its lead from the US."

He also took a cautious position on B.A.T. Industries. "The trouble with litigation is that you never know what basis people are going to settle, so despite having a large business outside the US and a relatively small one in it you are still in the arena."
As yet there is no indication of British pension fund trustees considering similar moves, fund managers said. -- James Saft, London newsroom +171 542 2734
